title: Goodnight, Goodnight, Construction Site
author: Sherri Duskey Rinker

hero.name: Construction Site (generic crane truck)
hero.description: Yellow crane truck on a construction site at dusk, the iconic cover image — no single named character but the crane truck is the most recognisable cover image
hero.source_note: Use generic yellow crane or construction truck from Boardmaker library; 'crane' symbol should work

ambiguous.issue: crane can mean the construction machine or the bird
ambiguous.reason: Book is about construction vehicles; machine meaning is correct — use construction crane search term

ambiguous.issue: could map to colour swatch (dark shade) or to darkness/night setting
ambiguous.reason: In this book dark describes the night-time setting when the trucks go to sleep — a scene/environment meaning, not a colour chip

ambiguous.issue: big is a general adjective that could map to a size comparison symbol or a large generic object
ambiguous.reason: Central to the book — construction vehicles are repeatedly described as big and powerful; standard size-adjective symbol is correct

notes: This book has no single named protagonist — the five trucks (Crane Truck, Cement Mixer, Dump Truck, Excavator, Bulldozer) are all central characters. The hero slot uses the crane truck as the most cover-recognisable vehicle. Four of the five trucks (excavator, dump truck, cement mixer, bulldozer) are included as fringe words; crane is covered by the hero slot, saving a fringe slot. Key theme words chosen are night, dark, loud, big, shovel, sun and moon to support the bedtime/goodnight narrative arc. Words like 'work', 'sleep', 'tired', and 'goodnight' are already in aac_extras and do not need to be duplicated in fringe. 'Hard hat', 'dirt', 'wheel', and 'bucket' are already in activity_images and are also omitted from fringe to avoid duplication.
